name: People's rights over their own data

failureModes.prompt: When someone deletes their account, must their data also leave backups, analytics and outside services within a stated time?
failureModes.why: copies in backups or outside tools leave a deletion incomplete, and India's DPDP Act and the EU GDPR both give a right to erasure

options.label: Everywhere, within a stated window
options.consequence: needs a list of every place data goes, and the promise can be kept

options.label: Only from the main database
options.consequence: quick to build, and copies remain in backups and other companies' systems

failureModes.provenBy: a written list of every place personal data is copied, and a test that deletes an account and asserts each place is cleared or scheduled within the window

failureModes.prompt: When someone deletes their account, what should happen to things they shared with other people?
failureModes.why: the answer decides who owns shared items, and that is hard to change once people depend on them

options.label: Keep shared items, without their name
options.consequence: others keep what they rely on, and the person's name is removed

options.label: Delete everything they made
options.consequence: the cleanest erasure, and other people lose work they depended on

failureModes.recommended: Keep shared items, without their name
failureModes.provenBy: a test that deletes one member of a shared space and asserts the shared items remain without that person's name

failureModes.prompt: Should we keep a dated record of what each person agreed to?
failureModes.why: the DPDP Act of 2023 in India and the GDPR in the EU require a business to be able to prove consent was given

options.label: Keep a dated record of each agreement
options.consequence: a small table, and we can show exactly what someone agreed to and when

options.label: Store only the current setting
options.consequence: simpler, and we cannot prove what someone agreed to last year

failureModes.recommended: Keep a dated record of each agreement
failureModes.provenBy: a test that changes a person's consent twice and asserts both dated entries and the policy version they agreed to are kept

failureModes.prompt: Before deleting an account or sending an export, should we confirm it is really the owner asking?
failureModes.why: deletion cannot be undone and an export contains everything, so a request from someone else's unlocked phone does the most damage here

options.label: Confirm again before acting
options.consequence: one extra step, and a stolen session cannot erase or copy the account

options.label: Act on the signed-in request
options.consequence: smoother, and anyone holding an unlocked phone can delete or export everything

failureModes.provenBy: a test that requests deletion and export from a session without fresh confirmation and asserts both are refused

failureModes.prompt: Should an export include only what the person created, or also items others shared with them?
failureModes.why: an export that includes other people's words gives their data to someone they did not choose

options.label: Only what they created or own
options.consequence: nothing private of anyone else leaves, and shared items are missing from it

options.label: Everything they can see
options.consequence: complete for them, and other people's content leaves with it

failureModes.recommended: Only what they created or own
failureModes.provenBy: a test that exports one member's data from a shared space and asserts no item created by another person is included

failureModes.prompt: After someone asks to delete their account, should there be a short period when they can cancel the request?
failureModes.why: a mistaken tap or a stolen phone can delete years of someone's work, and a short delay lets them undo it

options.label: A short grace period, then full deletion
options.consequence: accidental deletions can be reversed, and data stays for that period

options.label: Delete immediately
options.consequence: the simplest promise, and a mistaken tap is permanent

failureModes.recommended: A short grace period, then full deletion
failureModes.provenBy: a test that requests deletion, cancels inside the period and asserts the account is intact, then asserts full deletion after the period ends
